title: Electronic signatures and records in commerce (E-SIGN Act)
rule: In a transaction affecting interstate commerce, a signature, contract or record may not be denied legal effect solely because it is electronic, and a contract is not unenforceable solely because electronic signatures or records formed it. No one must agree to use or accept them. Where a law requires written information for a consumer, an electronic record counts only with the consumer's affirmative consent and required disclosures. A state that enacts the Uniform Electronic Transactions Act may displace these rules.
